summary: Iteration 8 backend testing complete. All new features (Report a profile, Language Filter, Live Support Chat with AI) work as specified. 24/24 pytest tests passing. One important false-positive bug discovered in the racist language filter (substring matching).

minor.issue: RACIST_WORDS check uses plain substring match (`word in text_lower`) instead of word-boundary matching. This produces false positives that will block legitimate user input. Verified examples: 'suspicious' is flagged because it contains 'spic'; same will happen for 'Pakistani' (contains 'paki'), 'Hispanic'/'auspicious' (contains 'spic'), 'Japan'/'Japanese' (contains 'jap'), 'crackers'/'nutcracker' (contains 'cracker'), 'wogan' (contains 'wog'). PROFANITY_WORDS correctly uses word-split match, but RACIST_WORDS does not. Recommended fix: use a regex with word boundaries (e.g. `re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(word)}\b', text)`), or at minimum split-by-non-alpha and compare. Currently this could prevent students reporting profiles, updating bios, sending support messages, etc. that contain perfectly legitimate words.

action_items: FIX FALSE POSITIVE in RACIST_WORDS filter: substring matching blocks legitimate words like 'suspicious' (matches 'spic'), 'Pakistani' (matches 'paki'), 'Japanese' (matches 'jap'), 'Hispanic' (matches 'spic'), 'crackers' (matches 'cracker'). Use word-boundary regex (re.search(r'\b{word}\b', text, re.IGNORECASE)) for racist terms, same as profanity already does. This affects ALL endpoints using check_language_filter (reports, profile bio/course/university, swipe comments, chat, support). Apply the same fix to the 'normalized' substring check (which currently substitutes 1->i, 0->o, etc. and then does substring search).

rca_of_issue: False-positive racism filter: in /app/backend/helpers/safeguarding.py line 111-113, RACIST_WORDS uses `if word in text_lower or word in normalized:` (substring match). PROFANITY_WORDS at line 123-126 correctly tokenises with `text_lower.split()`. Reproduction: POST /api/reports with reason='looks suspicious' returns 400 'racist or discriminatory'. Mitigation: replace with regex word-boundary match `re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(word)}\b', text_lower)` (and same against normalized). Apply across all callers automatically since they go through this helper.
